newsitem.title: USA: Yellowstone rangers resume capture of roaming bison.
newsitem.headline: Yellowstone rangers resume capture of roaming bison.

text.p: The Yellowstone National Park said Monday it resumed capturing bison at the northern edge of the park because heavy snows forced too many into the area in search of food.

The big, shaggy animals, also known as buffalo, can weigh as much as one ton and sprint at a speed of 30 miles per hour. They have been migrating toward the park's northern border and into areas in Montana where cattle graze.

Bison carry brucellosis, a disease that if spread to cattle can cause spontaneous abortion. Some 700 bison have been sent to slaughterhouses under a programme to keep them out of grazing areas in Montana.
Two weeks ago the park stopped capturing the bison and instead tried chasing them back into the park. As their numbers rose it became increasingly difficult to move them, park officials said.
When the hazing operation failed, park rangers resumed capturing the bison.
The captured animals will be tested for brucellosis. Those that test positive will be sent to slaughter and those that test negative will be held in a facility at the park.

On Friday, Department of Interior and Agriculture Department officials made a proposal to Montana that provided additional winter range for the animals on National Forest lands and indicated new flexibility about bison and cattle co-mingling.
